skill.name: planner
skill.description: Creates detailed implementation plans for bugs, features, and technical tasks using research, clarification, phased sprints, atomic tasks, validation, and risk analysis.
skill.summary: Turn technical requests into phased, testable implementation plans with clear dependencies and acceptance criteria.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives caused by ordinary prose and Markdown backticks. The skill contains no executable commands, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or malicious semantic intent.

static_findings.snippet: This will narrow and aid you in finding the right docs.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 88 uses inline Markdown backticks to format the literal filename suffix `-plan.md`. It does not contain Ruby, shell syntax, or an executable command.
Line 91 formats an example output filename with Markdown backticks. The text describes filename generation and performs no command execution.
Lines 103 through 147 are a fenced Markdown plan template. The fence declares Markdown content and contains no shell or Ruby instructions.
Line 33 explains that requirement clarification helps identify relevant documentation. It neither requests system information nor directs environment reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Complex technical requests can hide dependencies, risks, and unclear requirements. This skill produces phased plans with atomic tasks, acceptance criteria, and validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Investigates architecture, dependencies, related components, and existing implementation patterns.
Generates focused clarification questions before documentation research.
Organizes work into phased sprints with demo and verification checklists.
Breaks implementation into atomic, committable, and independently testable tasks.
Records task locations, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation methods.
Adds testing, rollback, risk, and gotcha sections to the final plan.
limitations: Creates plans only and does not implement the requested changes.
Depends on available codebase context and accurate answers to clarification questions.
Requires the separate Context7 skill for current external documentation.
Complexity labels and task sequencing remain estimates until implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature
use_cases.description: Convert a feature request into sequenced sprints, atomic tasks, tests, and rollout considerations.

use_cases.title: Scope a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Trace a reported defect through likely components and define focused investigation, repair, and regression testing tasks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Delivery Work
use_cases.description: Create a reviewable delivery plan with dependencies, demonstrations, risks, and acceptance criteria for team coordination.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for [small change]. Ask essential clarification questions, then provide atomic tasks with acceptance criteria and validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a focused code change

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the investigation and repair of [bug]. Include affected areas, likely causes, regression tests, risks, and rollback steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate defect analysis and remediation planning

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cross-System Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased plan for [feature] across [systems]. Map dependencies, integrations, permissions, data changes, tests, deployment, and sprint demonstrations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a High-Risk Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a phased migration plan from [current state] to [target state]. Include prerequisites, compatibility checks, observability, rollback gates, and parallel work.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert planning for complex and high-risk delivery

output_examples.input: Plan adding Google sign-in to an existing web application.
output_examples.output: A phased plan covering provider configuration, callback routing, user mapping, interface changes, security checks, integration tests, deployment, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Plan a fix for duplicate payment webhook processing.
output_examples.output: An investigation and repair plan covering reproduction, idempotency storage, concurrency behavior, regression tests, monitoring, deployment checks, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Plan migrating a shared API client to a new major version.
output_examples.output: A staged migration plan covering usage discovery, compatibility changes, incremental adoption, contract tests, observability, release gates, and cleanup.

best_practices: Provide business goals, technical constraints, and measurable success criteria.
Answer clarification questions before requesting the final plan.
Review task dependencies, validation steps, and rollback assumptions with implementers.
anti_patterns: Do not request a final plan while critical requirements remain unknown.
Do not treat estimated complexity or sequencing as confirmed implementation facts.
Do not use the plan as a substitute for testing, review, or deployment controls.

faq.question: Does this skill implement the plan?
faq.answer: No. It creates and saves the implementation plan but does not modify product code.

faq.question: What types of work can it plan?
faq.answer: It can plan bugs, features, migrations, integrations, and other technical tasks.

faq.question: Will it inspect my codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews relevant architecture, patterns, dependencies, and components when that context is available.

faq.question: Why does it ask clarification questions?
faq.answer: Clarification reduces ambiguity and helps align scope, constraints, risks, and success criteria.

faq.question: How are external libraries handled?
faq.answer: The skill requests current official documentation through Context7 when external dependencies are involved.

faq.question: What does the final plan contain?
faq.answer: It contains an overview, prerequisites, phased sprints, atomic tasks, acceptance criteria, validation, testing, risks, and rollback guidance.
